claim: Calibrate preflight conflict-level escalation: bare tag-overlap with a contract-grade node currently escalates a proposal to a contract-level block, costing an adjudication interrupt on genuinely disjoint matches - every dag-schema-tagged proposal hits the same multi-contract wall and receives the same boilerplate review. Decide and encode the criteria for when overlap warrants blocking versus informational priority (for example: require claim-overlap or subject-overlap in addition to a shared tag before contract-level), and land the change as a preflight-bucketing revision with a b055-family supersession if the scope doctrine moves.

evidence.detail: Grounded in the adjudication machinery's first live user-decision exercise (the thread-backlog close, b517/b518): both contract-level blocks were bare tag-overlap escalations, one against a genuinely disjoint match, costing a user interrupt the calibration would have avoided. Corroborated by a week of identical reviews: every plan-0-onward dag-schema proposal triggered the same wall and the same overlap-is-necessary-but-not-sufficient boilerplate. Surfaced in the closing report of that thread and minted here per /end step 8 (the close sweeps itself). Adjacent to b494 (consensual primitives / supportive-match handling), deliberately separate from it. Preflight 2026-06-11: one non-contract tag-overlap (backlog family sibling); notably the calibration directive itself cleared without a contract-level wall - tagged by concern (preflight, calibration) rather than dag-schema, which is itself a data point for the calibration: the escalation tracks the tag, not the content.

Second specimen within hours of authoring: cb:b062's preflight returned 17 contract / 35 schema hits, every one bare tag_overlap from the dag-schema family; the single true match (cb:b061, the supersession target) carried claim_overlap. Signal-to-noise 1:51; reviewed per b055 and proceeded on the b494 precedent (postscript 8).

Third specimen, with a wrinkle that cuts the other way: the b526/b527 preflight (the b511 discharge) returned 17 contract / 35 schema hits, all bare tag_overlap from a dag-schema tag - but this time the tag was semantically wrong on the proposal (the anchored-position format is document schema, not DAG-node schema), and the wall prompted the correction before import; under b511's own positions/schema/anchoring family the matches collapsed to zero in every conflict bucket. Calibration data point: the escalation tracks the tag, and exactly because it does, a contract-level wall on a mis-tagged proposal had diagnostic value once. The one genuine flag in the batch (b473 vs b528) was naming-tag overlap with no semantic contact, user-adjudicated proceed-unchanged.

Discharged 2026-06-12 (materialized t0015/t0016): the calibration decided and landed. Criteria encoded as cb:b064 (preflight-escalation-criteria, contract-grade audit-rule, deps b055 + this node): escalation into a conflict bucket requires semantic contact (subject_overlap or claim_overlap) alongside the contract-grade or dag-schema trigger; bare tag overlap re-buckets to neutral with the candidate's grade annotated in the render, preserving the evidence-3 mis-tag diagnostic without the wall. CB.Belief.Conflict.classify/2 gained semantic_contact?/1; 311 tests passing, schema verify 20/20. No b055-family supersession: the scope doctrine did not move - b055's overlap-is-necessary-but-not-sufficient invariant is now enforced mechanically at preflight instead of delegated to reviewer boilerplate. b064's own preflight was the calibrated bucketing's first live run: 0 contract, 0 schema, 3 neutral, with b055 surfacing as annotated neutral where the old code would have blocked.

todos.action: Recalibrate preflight bucketing in CB.Belief.Conflict: contract-grade or dag-schema-tagged matches classify as conflicting only with semantic contact (claim_overlap or subject_overlap among the match reasons); bare tag_overlap downgrades to neutral with the candidate's grade still annotated in the rendered output. Update moduledocs and tests.
todos.notes: b519's three specimens: every contract-level block in the thread-backlog close and the b062/b526 preflights was bare tag_overlap (signal-to-noise 1:51 on b062); the one mis-tag diagnostic (evidence 3) is preserved by keeping downgraded matches visible with grade annotation rather than suppressing them.

todos.action: Encode the escalation criteria as a contract-grade audit-rule node through the write flow (preflight, adjudicate, import), deps cb:b055 and cb:b519. No b055 supersession: its overlap-is-necessary-but-not-sufficient invariant is what the calibration enforces at preflight time.
todos.notes: b519 conditions the b055-family supersession on the scope doctrine moving; it does not - preflight stops delegating the insufficiency to reviewer boilerplate and enforces it mechanically instead.
